title: OKDP platform values
description: The settings of global.okdp the OKDP compiler reads, given by the context's values layers, the platform's at level 0 (platform.yaml, Inputs.Context). Every compile checks them, in every mode, and reports every violation at once; it applies the defaults. Only the settings the compiler reads are described: any other key is allowed (ingress.className, project...) but certificateIssuers, a former setting, refused (false): its selfSigned.name is tls.clusterIssuer. Every key reaches the mapping as written (global.okdp) and every chart (global). As in a chart's values, a null deletes a setting's default, and is refused where there is none; an empty string is a value.

suffix.description: The domain of the platform's hosts, which the mappings build the services' hosts with (a package requires it: require).

annotations.description: Annotations of every service's ingress, those the cluster's ingress controller reads (Traefik's middlewares, HAProxy's timeouts...): platform.ingressAnnotations, merged over cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer. Absent: none.

tls.description: The platform's certificates, whichever cert-manager and trust tool run on the cluster: OKDP's or the cluster's own.

clusterIssuer.description: The cert-manager ClusterIssuer of the services' certificates (OKDP's self-signed CA, an ACME or a corporate one): platform.ingressAnnotations, cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer. Absent: "".

caBundleSecret.description: The Secret of each namespace that holds the platform's CA bundle, ca.crt (PEM) and bundle.p12 (PKCS#12), as a trust-manager Bundle writes one, whichever tool fills it: the packages mount it to trust the platform's certificates, and the oidc-dcr Jobs by default (oidc.dcr.caSecret). Absent: the platform's certificates are trusted without a bundle (public CAs).

charts.description: The upstream charts that render the charts the compiler adds itself, each a repository, a chart and its version. Each is checked after the requirements as a dependency of Chart.yaml is: a repository URL, the name of a chart, a pinned version.

oidcDcr.description: The chart of the OAuth clients in dcr mode: an oidc-dcr chart that takes the values of oidc-dcr 0.5.0, which the compiler writes. Absent: oci://quay.io/adaltas, oidc-dcr, 0.5.0.

repository.description: The URL of the chart repository: https://, http:// or oci://.

chart.description: The name of the chart in the repository.

version.description: A pinned version (1.2.3), not a range.

oidc.description: The platform's identity provider, and how the services' OAuth clients are provisioned. The mapping sees it as platform.oidc, defaults applied, with existing and dcr.enabled, the mode in effect.

enabled.description: Whether the services use OIDC. A null deletes the default: OIDC is off, and platform.oidc.enabled is absent.

clientProvisioning.description: How the services' OAuth clients are provisioned. existing: by the platform, each client's Secret creds-<release>-oauth2[-<name>]. dcr: each registered by dynamic client registration, by the Job of an oidc-dcr chart the compiler adds, its Secret <release>-<namespace>[-<name>]-dcr.

scope.description: The scope a client registers in dcr mode when it sets none (openid left out).

issuerUri.description: The provider's issuer URL: the oidc-dcr Jobs wait for its discovery document, <issuerUri>/.well-known/openid-configuration (waitForProvider.discoveryUrl).

dcr.description: The settings of the oidc-dcr Jobs that register the OAuth clients in dcr mode: the values of the client charts. The mapping sees them as platform.oidc.dcr, defaults applied.

registrationUrl.description: The registration endpoint the Jobs register the clients at (registrationUrl). Required, a non-empty string, in dcr mode when a service declares a client: checked then only.

authMethod.description: How the Jobs authenticate to the registration endpoint: anonymous, the only method OKDP supports. Required in dcr mode when a service declares a client: checked then only.

image.description: The Jobs' image (registry, repository, tag, pullPolicy, pullSecrets), merged over the chart's: the camelCase keys of oidc-dcr >= 0.5.0, the snake_case keys of an earlier version, pull_policy and pull_secrets, refused. Absent: the chart's.

caSecret.description: The Secret holding the CA bundle the Jobs trust (tls.certificate); a client's caSecret wins. Absent: tls.caBundleSecret, else ""; "": none, the Jobs trusting their image's CAs.

ttlSeconds.description: How long a finished Job, and its logs, is kept, in seconds (ttlSeconds).

waitTtlSeconds.description: The longest wait for the provider's discovery document, in seconds (waitForProvider.ttlSeconds); the Jobs wait only when oidc.issuerUri is set. Absent: the chart's, 600.

proxy.description: The platform's proxy: platform.proxyEnv, the environment variables of each setting that is not empty.

provisioning.description: The classes of the claims, by contract, as Kubernetes' storage classes: each class the provider of its claims and what it fixes of their request, one of them the default class, of the claims that name neither a class nor a provider. A claim names a class (class), or its provider (provider), or takes the default class; one that names neither, without a default class, is refused. The platform gives its classes and the default (platform.yaml); a project adds classes of its own (project.yaml), and the default of a contract the platform leaves without one, and changes none of the platform's: a class and a default are each taken whole. The platform's classes route every namespace to their providers; a project's reaches a provider of another namespace with its consent only, the claimers of the provider's instance.yaml, else of its package's provisions, listing the project. Never an instance.

default.description: The default class of the contract: a class of classes, the one of the claims that name neither a class nor a provider. Set once, at the lowest level that sets it: a project that wants another provider adds a class and names it.

classes.description: The classes of the contract, by name, a DNS-1123 label: another name is refused.

^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$.description: A class: the provider of its claims, and what it fixes of their request.

provider.description: The instance that provisions the claims of the class: <namespace>/<name>, or <name> of the claimer's namespace, the name the instance's name or its release. Of another namespace than the claimer's, it serves a class of the platform's (level 0), and a project's only when its claimers list the claimer's namespace, or *.

request.description: What the class fixes of the request of each of its claims, checked with it against the contract's claim schema (x-okdp-claim): a claim that sets one of its keys is refused.

secrets.description: The platform's secret store: where secrets go between namespaces, and where connections may keep their credentials.

store.description: The name of the secret store of External Secrets the credentials of a claim bound across namespaces go through: its provider pushes them (a PushSecret, deleted from the store with the claim), its claimers read them (an ExternalSecret), under the key <provider's namespace>/<claim ID>, the ID starting with the claimers' namespace, a property per secret field of the contract: a path-based store (OpenBao, Vault, a cloud secret manager) scopes a writer by the first segment and a reader by the first label of the second; the platform's own keys are under platform/, a namespace no project may have. Required by such a claim whose output has a secretRef. A connection whose secretRef is {remoteKey: <key>} keeps its credentials there, under that key: each instance that references it reads them (an ExternalSecret) into a Secret of its namespace, <release>.<connection>-credentials. Required by such a connection.

provider.description: The provider of the store, External Secrets' SecretStore spec.provider, verbatim (vault: an OpenBao or Vault server, its KV v2 mount, its Kubernetes auth, whose serviceAccountRef names serviceAccount). Set, the store is a SecretStore of that name in each project's namespace, which the targets write with the ServiceAccount serviceAccount, and the PushSecrets and ExternalSecrets reference it (kind SecretStore): the store's policy scopes each namespace by the identity it authenticates with. Unset, the store is a ClusterSecretStore of that name the platform created, one identity for every namespace: one trust domain.

serviceAccount.description: With provider: the ServiceAccount of each project's namespace the store authenticates with, the one provider's serviceAccountRef names.

refreshInterval.description: How often the PushSecrets push the credentials of the claims across namespaces to the store, and the ExternalSecrets read them, and those of the connections kept in it (refreshInterval, a duration): rotated credentials reach their claimers within it.

policy.description: The platform's policy: what the projects may deploy, and which projects are the platform's own.

privileged.description: The namespaces of the platform's own projects (cert-manager, ingress-nginx, an operator...), whose instances install cluster-scoped objects, write other namespaces and set any upstream value, as the other projects may not; the targets give their releases the engine's own identity, the other projects' one confined to their namespace (Result.Privileged).
